text:
LangChain & LangGraph Migration Guide
Migration knowledge document for testing an autonomous Python code migration agent.
Purpose
This document contains explicit migration rules. A migration agent should extract these rules from the
documentation, identify matching constructs in Python source code, retrieve supporting documentation, and
apply transformations without inventing unsupported rules.
Rule 1 — OpenAI LLM import
Legacy:
 from langchain.llms import OpenAI
Modern:
 from langchain_openai import OpenAI
Migration note: Apply this rule only when the source construct matches the documented legacy form.
Rule 2 — ChatOpenAI import
Legacy:
 from langchain.chat_models import ChatOpenAI
Modern:
 from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

Rule 11 — LLM chains
Legacy:

Modern:
 Use an LCEL RunnableSequence pipeline instead of the legacy LLMChain abstraction.
Migration note: Apply this rule only when the source construct matches the documented legacy form.
Rule 12 — Agent initialization
Legacy:

Modern:
 Use create_agent from langchain.agents for the current agent API.
Migration note: Apply this rule only when the source construct matches the documented legacy form.
Rule 13 — LangGraph ReAct agent
Legacy:

Modern:
 Use the current LangChain/LangGraph agent API; do not introduce new code using the
deprecated prebuilt helper.

Example Combined Migration
Legacy code:
 from langchain.chat_models import ChatOpenAI
from langchain.embeddings import OpenAIEmbeddings
from langchain.vectorstores import FAISS
from langchain.text_splitter import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
llm = ChatOpenAI()
embeddings = OpenAIEmbeddings()
vectorstore = FAISS.from_documents([], embeddings)
splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(chunk_size=500)
Expected migrated imports:
 from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI, OpenAIEmbeddings
from langchain_community.vectorstores import FAISS
from langchain_text_splitters import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
Agent Behavior Requirements
 Extract only migration rules explicitly supported by this document.
 Do not infer or invent a replacement when the document does not provide one.
 A CST node becomes a migration candidate when it matches an extracted rule.

 A CST node becomes a migration candidate when it matches an extracted rule.
 Use semantic retrieval to obtain supporting documentation for a candidate.
 Use the LLM to reason about the exact transformation, then apply the approved transformation with LibCST.
 Preserve program behavior, comments, and unrelated identifiers whenever possible.
